Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.webbrowser

Class EncodingFallback

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.webbrowser.EncodingFallback
public final class EncodingFallback extends Object
Pure helpers behind the Web Browser's blank-page workaround.

JavaFX 21's WebKit loader (com.sun.webkit.network.HTTP2Loader) can only decode Content-Encoding: gzip and deflate. When a site answers with any other token -- Brotli, zstd, or a non-standard none -- the loader logs "Unknown encoding type '...' found, discarding" at SEVERE and throws the body away, so the load worker still reports SUCCEEDED but the page renders completely blank. This is an engine limitation that is only fixed in JavaFX 24+ (which needs JDK 22+, beyond this port's JDK 21 pin), so it cannot be patched at the source.

The workaround re-fetches such a page with the JDK java.net.http client -- which, unlike WebKit, does not advertise Accept-Encoding and so is normally answered with a plain identity body, and can decode gzip / deflate itself when it is not. This class holds every decision that does not need JavaFX so it is unit-tested headlessly: detecting the discarded body from a cheap DOM probe, decoding the transported Content-Encoding, choosing a charset, and re-injecting a <base> tag so the recovered document's relative links and images still resolve against the origin (a WebEngine.loadContent document has no base URL of its own).

  • Method Details

    • parseProbe

      public static int[] parseProbe(String raw)
      Parses the "elementCount:textLength" string returned by the DOM probe script. Tolerant of null / malformed input so a failed script can never be mistaken for a blank page.
      Parameters:
      raw - the probe result (may be null)
      Returns:
      a two-element array {elementCount, textLength}, or {-1, -1} when the probe could not be read

    • isBlankDom

      public static boolean isBlankDom(int elementCount, int textLength)
      True when a finished document is an empty skeleton with no text: the signature of a body WebKit discarded for an undecodable Content-Encoding. A negative (unknown) count never matches.
      Parameters:
      elementCount - the number of elements in the document
      textLength - the trimmed length of the body's text content
      Returns:
      true when the page should be treated as blank

    • decode

      public static byte[] decode(byte[] body, String contentEncoding) throws IOException
      Decodes a transported body according to its Content-Encoding. Identity, the non-standard none, gzip and deflate are handled; any other token (Brotli, zstd, ...) is beyond this build and raises an IOException so the caller can present an honest error page.
      Parameters:
      body - the raw response bytes (may be null)
      contentEncoding - the response's Content-Encoding header (may be null)
      Returns:
      the decoded bytes, never null
      Throws:
      IOException - when the encoding is unsupported or the body is corrupt

    • charsetFor

      public static Charset charsetFor(String contentType)
      Resolves the charset named by a Content-Type header, defaulting to UTF-8 when it is absent, malformed or unknown to this JVM.
      Parameters:
      contentType - the response's Content-Type header (may be null)
      Returns:
      the charset to decode the body with, never null

    • injectBaseTag

      public static String injectBaseTag(String html, String baseUrl)
      Injects a <base href="url"> tag so a document rendered with WebEngine.loadContent (which has no base URL) still resolves its relative links, scripts and images against the original origin. A document that already declares a <base> is returned unchanged; when there is no <head> one is synthesised right after <html>, and with neither the tag is simply prepended.
      Parameters:
      html - the recovered markup (may be null)
      baseUrl - the origin URL to make relative references resolve against
      Returns:
      the markup with a base tag ensured, never null

    • describe

      public static String describe(Throwable t)
      A short, human-readable description of a decoding failure, used as the detail line of the fallback error page.
      Parameters:
      t - the failure (may be null)
      Returns:
      a non-null message
